newsitem.title: USA: Muni insurance Q1 volume up two pct -- Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Muni insurance Q1 volume up two pct -- Reuter poll.

text.p: Municipal bond insurance companies backed $20.4 billion of bonds in the first quarter of 1997, or 54 percent of all bonds sold during the period, according to a Reuters poll of the industry.

MBIA Insurance Corp., a unit of MBIA Inc., was again the market share leader for the period, insuring $8.4 billion of bonds or 41 percent of the insured market. The company's volume was essentially unchanged from the first quarter 1996 results, however.
In a rare shake-up of the market share rankings, Financial Guaranty Insurance Co. took the second-place spot away from AMBAC Inc.'s AMBAC Indemnity Corp. unit.
FGIC, a unit of General Electric Co.'s GE Capital Services, saw its volume jump 33 percent to $4.9 billion from $3.7 billion, for a 24 percent market share.
AMBAC's market share was 22 percent, as volume fell 19 percent to $4.4 billion from $5.5 billion.

Financial Security Assurance, a unit of Financial Security Assurance Holdings Ltd., insured $2.6 billion of bonds in the period, an 18.2 percent increase over the same period last year for a 13 percent market share.
Rounding out the list was Connie Lee Insurance Co., which insured $70 million of bonds during the period, compared to $153 million in the first three months of 1996.
